# B4R_SCHEMA_CONFORMANCE

**I-08B3.1-B4R — OFFICIAL DTCG 2025.10 SCHEMA VALIDATION.** Machine-generated by
`tools/b4-results.mjs` from `schema.json`, which `tools/b4r-schema.mjs` wrote. No figure is typed.

## 1. The authority, and why it is vendored

| | |
|---|---|
| official base | `https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/` |
| vendored from | `https://github.com/design-tokens/community-group` — *the official DTCG repository for the design tokens site and specification* |
| report pinned to | `f0f32a7dce0b (2025-10-28, "Publish 2025.10" #340)` |
| schema sources at | `11f95e87701e (2026-06-09, "Bundle JSON schema" #412) - the last commit to touch schemas/src/2025.10/resolver*` |
| files | 22, dialect draft-07 |
| retrieved | 2026-09-21 |
| validator | **ajv** — a third-party JSON Schema implementation |

`designtokens.org` is unreachable from this environment on every transport tried, so the schema is
**pinned with provenance** rather than fetched at validation time — which is also what the
independent review asked for. Every vendored file carries its SHA-256 **and its git blob SHA-1**,
recomputed locally and matched against the blob sha the GitHub tree API reports for the official
repository. S-01 re-checks all of it before any document is validated, because a vendored authority
that can be edited is not an authority — and an edited schema would make every check below pass for
the wrong reason, which is the most comfortable failure available to this package.

| **S-02** The resolver document is VALID against the official DTCG 2025.10 Resolver Schema | PASS | valid against `https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/resolver.json` (draft-07, resolved through its 3 sub-schemas), validated by ajv - a third-party implementation this package did not author |
| **S-03** Every shipped token file is VALID against the official DTCG 2025.10 Format Schema | PASS | 6 token files valid against `https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/format.json`, including the two value-free appearance sets and the canonical deliverable |
| **S-04** The document declares the schema it is actually valid against | PASS | `$schema` is `https://www.designtokens.org/schemas/2025.10/resolver.json`, and that id is the `$id` of the vendored file `schemas/2025.10/resolver.json` which S-02 validated against |
| **S-05** The official schema and the custom validator do not disagree | PASS | both accept the shipped resolver document; no disagreement to resolve |

| probe | official schema | custom V-11 | result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `s-n0` THE DOCUMENT B4 SHIPPED | REJECT *(exp. REJECT; 17 err)* | REJECT *(exp. REJECT; 2 err)* | PASS |
| `s-nA` PROBE A - `sets` as an array | REJECT *(exp. REJECT; 1 err)* | REJECT *(exp. REJECT; 1 err)* | PASS |
| `s-nB` PROBE B - `modifiers` as an array | REJECT *(exp. REJECT; 1 err)* | REJECT *(exp. REJECT; 1 err)* | PASS |
| `s-nC` PROBE C - `{ type, name }` in resolutionOrder for a ROOT-declared set | REJECT *(exp. REJECT; 15 err)* | REJECT *(exp. REJECT; 3 err)* | PASS |
| `s-nD` PROBE D - `$ref` to an undeclared set | ACCEPT *(exp. ACCEPT; 0 err)* | REJECT *(exp. REJECT; 1 err)* | PASS |
| `s-nE` PROBE E - modifier `default` naming a context it does not have | ACCEPT *(exp. ACCEPT; 0 err)* | REJECT *(exp. REJECT; 1 err)* | PASS |

**`s-n0` is not synthetic.** It is the resolver document **B4 actually shipped**, read from the
sealed package: **17 schema violations**, 2 from V-11.
First schema error: `/sets type: must be object`. If the corrected suite could not reject the
exact bytes that caused this revision, the correction would be a rewording.

## 4. What each validator is for

| | official JSON Schema | custom `validateResolver` (V-11) |
|---|---|---|
| owns | **syntax** — shapes, required members, `oneOf` forms, `const` version | **runtime obligations** the schema cannot express |
| authored by | DTCG | this package |
| catches probes | A, B, C | A, B, C, **D, E** |
| wins a disagreement | **yes, always, on syntax** | no |

The schema states in its own `$comment`, twice, that it cannot validate a `default` against its
`contexts`, nor uniqueness across array items; and it cannot know whether a `$ref` lands on a
declared set. So the two **partition** the specification. S-05 is the check that would report a
genuine disagreement instead of quietly resolving one.
